q: In Expo vs bare, what is the main question?
options: Who owns and keeps up the android and ios native folders
Whether the app can use Hermes
Whether the app can use React
why: Every app is your JavaScript plus the native projects. Expo (with CNG) generates the folders from config. Bare means you keep and edit them by hand.

q: Expo Go is a good base for a production app that goes to the store.
why: No. The Expo docs call Expo Go a limited playground. It has a fixed set of native code. A real app uses a development build, which holds your own native code.

q: Which of these are true about Continuous Native Generation (CNG)?
options: The android and ios folders are generated by prebuild
They are made from the app config, config plugins and a template
You should edit the generated folders by hand and keep the edits
A hand edit in a generated folder can be lost at prebuild --clean
why: Prebuild makes the folders from config, plugins and a template. The Expo docs warn that hand edits in them can be lost, so put the change in config or a config plugin.

q: Put these in the order a prebuild project uses them.
items: Write settings in app.json and add config plugins
Run npx expo prebuild to generate the android and ios folders
Build the app from the generated folders
Change a setting by editing app.json, then run prebuild again
why: Config first, then prebuild makes the folders, then you build. When something changes, you change the config and generate again, you do not edit the folders.

q: You have an old bare app with many hand made native changes. Which first step is safest for adopting Expo tools?
options: Install the expo package and move step by step, without running prebuild on the hand edited folders
Run npx expo prebuild --clean at once
Delete the android and ios folders
why: The Expo docs say Expo tools work in any React Native app, but prebuild may overwrite hand made changes. Move step by step, and later move each hand edit into a config plugin.

q: A development build is "your own version of Expo ______". (one word)
why: The Expo docs describe a development build as your own version of Expo Go, where you can use any native library and change native settings.
